academic_year_covered: 2026/2027 (program admission page updated for 2026; orientamento profile page states 'Updated on a.y. 2025/2026')
program_name: Civil and Environmental Engineering (Bachelor's Degree / Corso di Laurea, abbreviated 'L-CEE' on the department site). Standalone English-taught degree: the degree is awarded under this English name, it is not an English curriculum inside an Italian-named program.
teaching_language: English (100%). The orientamento course profile lists Language = 'ENG'. The program's own admission page states the course is taught in English and is part of the International Catalogue at Federico II. It appears in the university International Course Catalogue under '3-year Bachelor's degrees (L) > Engineering > Civil and Environmental Engineering - ENG' (no IT/ENG dual marking, unlike e.g. Hospitality Management). Because the program is delivered in English, non-EU applicants are NOT required to prove Italian at B2 (international.unina.it admission regulation, section 'Do I have to take the Italian language knowledge test?', point 2).
campus: Naples - Polo Ovest (Fuorigrotta engineering campus). All first-cycle lectures are held at Via Claudio 21, 80125 Napoli (seat of DICEA). Teaching departments: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Civile, Edile e Ambientale (DICEA) and Dipartimento di Strutture per l'Ingegneria e l'Architettura (DiSt). Enrolment / student office is at a different address: Segreteria Studenti Area Didattica Ingegneria, Piazzale Tecchio 80, 80125 Napoli. Note: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base engineering bachelors normally require students to choose Polo Est (San Giovanni a Teduccio) or Polo Ovest (Piazzale Tecchio, Via Claudio, Via Nuova Agnano, Monte Sant'Angelo) at matriculation; for this program the course page fixes teaching at Via Claudio (Polo Ovest).
degree_class: L-7 R (Italian degree class for Civil and Environmental Engineering). Stated as 'L-7 R' on the orientamento course profile and as 'Class L-7R' on the program admission page. [uncertain] The meaning of the 'R' suffix is not explained on any unina.it page found; an older official DICEA PDF (April 2024) writes the class simply as 'L7'.
admission_type: Open access (no numero programmato / no ranking-based selection) WITH a compulsory entry test and OFA mechanism. Multiple layers apply: (1) Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base classifies engineering bachelors of this kind as 'TA-OFA' = compulsory admission test, non-selective but triggering Additional Formative Obligations (OFA) if entry requirements are lacking; (2) the program's own page nevertheless calls it a 'compulsory selective test' with a hard minimum threshold of 20% of the maximum score required for enrolment; (3) non-EU applicants who need a visa face an ADDITIONAL document-based pre-admission selection assessed by the Degree Programme Coordinator, run through the Universitaly portal, before a pre-admission/offer letter is issued. The program is not listed among UNINA 'corsi a numero programmato' with an admission bando (the university bandi page currently shows no active call). Accepted entry credentials: CEnT-S (CISIA English test) from 2026, or SAT as an alternative; English TOLC-I was used up to the 2025/26 intake.
academic_requirements: 1) Upper-secondary school diploma. When the diploma was issued by a non-Italian school, the applicant must obtain a 'Dichiarazione di Valore' (Declaration of Value, DoV) from the Italian embassy/consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA statement of comparability, certifying that the diploma was obtained after AT LEAST 12 YEARS of pre-university education. 2) Both EU and non-EU candidates must demonstrate personal preparation in two areas: (a) logical ability - correctly interpreting a text, identifying the input data of a problem and using them to reach a solution, deducing the behaviour of a simple system, linking results to the hypotheses that determine them; (b) basic scientific knowledge - properties and operations on numbers, absolute value, powers and roots, logarithms and exponentials, literal calculus, polynomials, first- and second-degree algebraic equations and inequalities, systems of first-degree equations, measure and properties of segments and angles, lines and planes, properties of the main plane and solid geometric figures, Cartesian coordinates, concept of function, equations of lines and simple geometric loci, graphs and properties of elementary and trigonometric functions, elementary physics and basic knowledge of the structure of matter. 3) This preparation is verified by the compulsory entry test (see entry_exam_or_test). 4) Degree structure to be completed: 3 years, 180 CFU. 5) There is no prior-degree or minimum-GPA requirement; no interview and no portfolio are required.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 or higher is COMPULSORY for both EU and non-EU candidates, and must be evidenced by a certificate; the level is verified before enrolment by the University Language Centre (CLA, www.cla.unina.it). MOI (Medium of Instruction) certificates are explicitly NO LONGER accepted. Certifying bodies recognised by UNINA and listed on the program admission page: Cambridge Assessment English; City and Guilds (Pitman); Edexcel/Pearson Ltd; Educational Testing Service (ETS); English Speaking Board (ESB); IELTS; Pearson; Trinity College London; Department of English, Faculty of Arts - University of Malta; NQAI-ACELS (Ireland); Ascentis; AIM Awards; Learning Resource Network (LRN); British Council EnglishScore; British Institutes; Gatehouse Awards Ltd; TOEFL; LanguageCert; ESaT Malta; AELS NOCN; Duolingo (with verification code). The page warns that if English proficiency is only tested AFTER enrolment, the visa procedure at embassies/consulates may fail - so the certificate should be in hand at pre-admission stage. Italian language: NOT required (no Italian B2), because the degree is delivered in English; the university admission regulation states that for English-taught first-cycle courses 'level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required'. [uncertain] No minimum numeric score per certificate (e.g. IELTS band, TOEFL score) is published on the unina.it pages - only the B2 CEFR level.
application_deadline_eu: No separate application/selection deadline: EU candidates (and non-EU candidates already holding an Italian study visa) go directly to the enrolment phase. Enrolment window announced by the program: opens 2026-07-15 and closes 2026-10-31, with a likely but not guaranteed extension to December ('Final enrollment starts on July 15th and ends on October 31th'). The Admission Schedule table on the same page phrases the same window as 'from July to the end of October (can be possibly delayed to December)'. Related university-wide dates for a.y. 2026/2027 (Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27): first-year bachelor matriculation payments open from 2026-07-16, first instalment due by 2026-11-02, second instalment by 2027-03-01. Classes: first term from mid-September 2026; second term from early March 2027. [uncertain] Conflict: the Scuola Politecnica page states that matriculation to engineering bachelors is allowed 'from 1 September' via the SegrePass online platform, whereas the program page gives 15 July as the start; also, foreign-citizen students (EU included) cannot use the online SegrePass procedure and must enrol in person at the Segreterie Studenti.
application_deadline_non_eu: Multi-stage, and the published dates are inconsistent between the program page and the central international office. (A) Program-level pre-admission selection (only for non-EU applicants residing abroad who need a visa): 'expected start Jan 2026', 'expected closing 31st May 2026' (2026-01 to 2026-05-31), run in selection groups via the intake webpage / Universitaly. (B) Universitaly pre-enrolment portal: the program page states that in 2025 it opened 2025-04-01 and closed 2025-05-31, and applicants must select University of Naples Federico II and the Bachelor's Degree in Civil and Environmental Engineering (Class L-7R). (C) Central international office (international.unina.it) publishes DIFFERENT university-wide deadlines for the same cycle: pre-enrolment application deadline to UNINA 2026-06-15 ('After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only'), and deadline for submitting the visa application at Italian embassies/consulates 2026-11-30. (D) Visa application: to be started soon after the pre-admission/offer letter is issued. (E) Final in-person enrolment in Naples: 2026-07-15 to 2026-10-31, possibly deferred to December. [uncertain] Applicants should treat 2026-05-31 (program pre-admission close) as the binding earlier deadline and 2026-06-15 as the university-wide outer limit; the discrepancy is not reconciled on any unina.it page.
required_documents: A) For the non-EU pre-admission selection (uploaded via the Universitaly portal / intake webpage, assessed by the Bachelor's Degree Coordinator): 1) Passport; 2) High School degree certificate (diploma obtained after at least 12 years of pre-university education); 3) DoV (Declaration of Value) issued by an Italian embassy/consulate, or a CIMEA comparability statement; 4) English language certificate at CEFR B2 or higher; 5) CEnT-S result with minimum score 11 out of 55. B) For final in-person enrolment at the Segreteria Studenti Area Didattica Ingegneria (Piazzale Tecchio 80, weekdays 09:00-12:00): 1) identity document/passport (shown + one copy left); 2) proof of payment of tuition fees (which for non-EU students coincide with the regional tax and the legal stamp); 3) passport-size photograph in .jpeg format; 4) visa permit (shown + one copy); 5) permit of stay (permesso di soggiorno); 6) copy of the pre-admission letter (shown + one copy); 7) Declaration of Value (DoV) or, alternatively, CIMEA certificate of comparability; 8) copy of the high school diploma (shown + one copy); 9) copy of the English language proficiency certificate; 10) the enrolment application form downloadable from the program site (All_4_DOM_IMM_CEE.pdf). The central international office additionally lists a tax code (codice fiscale) among documents required for enrolment. [uncertain] An older official DICEA PDF (pre-enrollment-procedure.pdf, April 2024) required a LONGER pre-admission dossier that the current live page no longer lists: Curriculum Vitae, motivation letter / statement of purpose, optional letters of recommendation, a third-party statement of sponsorship or private accommodation availability, and financial guarantee statement(s) for EUR 6,080.00 per year for three years. It is unclear whether these are still requested in practice at the pre-admission or visa stage.
entry_exam_or_test: Compulsory entry test, taken BEFORE enrolment, no interview and no portfolio. CURRENT RULE (from 2026): the English TOLC-I has been discontinued and replaced by the unified CEnT-S test (CISIA English test used by Italian universities for English-taught scientific degrees; 55 questions, maximum score 55). Minimum score required for enrolment: 11 out of 55, i.e. the stated 'minimum threshold of 20% of the maximum score for the test'. ALTERNATIVE (new, for a.y. 2026-27): the admission requirement can instead be met with an SAT score, accepted if larger than 20% of the maximum, i.e. at least 320 marks out of 1600. PREVIOUS RULE (up to and including the 2025/26 intake): English TOLC-I administered by the CISIA Consortium, taken remotely (TOLC@CASA) after registering on the CISIA website, and repeatable. OFA (Obblighi Formativi Aggiuntivi): admitted candidates who did not score more than 50% of the marks available in the Mathematics section (i.e. 10) AND at least 15 marks overall (out of the 50 available points) are assigned an OFA requiring them to acquire at least 9 CFU in the MATH-03/A subject area (former MAT/05) before being allowed to sit ANY other examination; the educational debt must in any case be cleared within the first year. [uncertain] Two unresolved inconsistencies: (1) the OFA thresholds are still written in TOLC-I terms (20-point Mathematics section, 50-point total) while the qualifying test is now CEnT-S with a 55-point maximum - the page does not restate the OFA thresholds on the CEnT-S scale; (2) the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base page still advertises TOLC-I (TOLC@CASA and TOLC@UNI, minimum score 15 excluding the English section) with 2026 session dates for a.y. 2026/2027 - most plausibly because TOLC-I remains the test for the Italian-taught engineering bachelors while CEnT-S covers the English-taught ones, but no unina.it page states this split explicitly.
tuition_or_fees_link: Main official links: https://www.unina.it/en/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (Registration and fees, English hub) | https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026 (Guida all'iscrizione a.a. 2026-27, authoritative) | http://calcolatrice.unina.it (official fee simulator) | https://www.unina.it/didattica/sportello-studenti/guide-dello-studente (student guides index) | program-level summary at https://www.civil-environmental.unina.it/admission/. SUMMARY per the 2026-27 Guida all'iscrizione: non-EU citizens are TOTALLY EXEMPT from the enrolment contribution and pay only the regional right-to-study tax plus the EUR 16.00 stamp duty; EU (non-Italian) citizens pay only a fixed contribution of EUR 200 (where the calculated contribution would be 200 or more) plus the regional tax and stamp duty. Regional right-to-study tax for 2026-27 is banded: EUR 130.00 (ISEEU up to EUR 25,500 and students from particularly poor countries), EUR 151.00 (ISEEU EUR 25,500.01-51,000 AND students whose household resides abroad), EUR 173.00 (ISEEU above EUR 51,000 or no ISEEU declaration). Payment is split into three instalments (60% + regional tax + stamp with the first). [uncertain] The program admission page still quotes an older flat figure of EUR 140/year regional tax (non-EU: EUR 140 + EUR 16 stamp; EU: EUR 200 + EUR 140 + EUR 16), which is superseded by the 130/151/173 banding in the 2026-27 guide - a student from a household resident abroad would fall in the EUR 151 band. Scholarships: ADISURC (Campania regional right-to-study body) runs an annual call, and the department awards 6 merit scholarships of EUR 1,000 each to regular students enrolling in the 2nd year before the end of October.
official_program_url: https://www.civil-environmental.unina.it/ (official degree programme website, DICEA) | https://www.orientamento.unina.it/corsidistudio/civil-and-environmental-engineering/ (official UNINA orientamento course profile) | https://www.civil-environmental.unina.it/admission/ (admission page) | https://www.international.unina.it/international-courses-catalogue/ (listing as an ENG bachelor)
official_call_url: No dedicated bando / rectoral decree exists for this program: it is an open-access course, and the university 'Corsi a numero programmato > Bandi di ammissione' page (http://www.unina.it/didattica/offerta-didattica/corsi-a-numero-programmato/bandi-di-ammissione) currently reports no new content, confirming this course is not admitted by competitive call. The governing official documents are instead: https://www.international.unina.it/education/admission-regulation/ (UNINA admission regulation for EU and non-EU students, the document the program page tells candidates to read) | https://www.unina.it/documents/11958/35974352/2023-03-21_notice_non_EU_Students.pdf (UNINA notice for non-EU students) | https://www.dicea.unina.it/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/pre-enrollment-procedure.pdf (DICEA pre-enrollment procedure, April 2024, now partly superseded). [uncertain]
seats_total: Not published. [uncertain] No seat cap or number of places is stated on the orientamento course profile, the program website, the DICEA pages or the international catalogue; this is consistent with the course being open access (not numero programmato), which in the Italian system normally means no fixed seat ceiling.
non_eu_reserved_seats: Not published. [uncertain] No non-EU quota ('contingente riservato') number for this program was found on any unina.it page, nor in the university bandi section (which is currently empty). Non-EU admission is instead gated by the document-based pre-admission selection assessed by the Degree Programme Coordinator, not by a published numeric quota.

uncertainty_notes: 1) ENTRY TEST CONFLICT (most important): the program's own admission page says the English TOLC-I was discontinued and replaced from 2026 by the CEnT-S test (min 11/55), while the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base page still advertises TOLC-I for a.y. 2026-2027 (TOLC@CASA / TOLC@UNI, min 15 excluding the English section) with 2026 session dates. The most plausible reading - TOLC-I for Italian-taught engineering bachelors, CEnT-S for the English-taught ones - is NOT stated on any unina.it page. The outline note for this item ('TOLC-I + OFA') is therefore outdated for the 2026/27 intake. 2) OFA THRESHOLD SCALE MISMATCH: the OFA rule is still expressed on the TOLC-I scale (Mathematics 10 out of 20, 15 out of 50 overall) even though CEnT-S has a 55-point maximum; the page does not restate the OFA thresholds on the CEnT-S scale. 3) NON-EU DEADLINE CONFLICT: program page gives pre-admission closing 2026-05-31 (and Universitaly 1 Apr - 31 May, quoted for 2025), while international.unina.it gives a university-wide pre-enrolment deadline of 2026-06-15 and an embassy visa-application deadline of 2026-11-30. 4) EU ENROLMENT START CONFLICT: program page says final enrolment starts 15 July; Scuola PSB says engineering matriculation opens 1 September via SegrePass; and foreign-citizen students (EU included) cannot use SegrePass at all and must enrol in person. 5) FEE FIGURES OUTDATED ON THE PROGRAM PAGE: it quotes a flat EUR 140/year regional tax, superseded by the 2026-27 banding of EUR 130 / 151 / 173; students with a household resident abroad fall in the EUR 151 band. The 'almost null tuition fees' claim for non-EU students is nonetheless confirmed by the official 2026-27 guide (total exemption from the enrolment contribution). 6) REQUIRED DOCUMENTS DRIFT: the April 2024 DICEA PDF required CV, motivation letter, recommendation letters, sponsorship/accommodation statement and a financial guarantee of EUR 6,080.00/year for three years; the current live page omits all of these. Unclear whether they are still requested at pre-admission or visa stage. The financial-guarantee figure in particular is likely still relevant for the visa but is no longer published. 7) SEATS: neither a total seat number nor a non-EU reserved quota is published anywhere on unina.it for this program; consistent with open access, but it means non-EU applicants cannot see how many are admitted. 8) DEGREE CLASS SUFFIX: 'L-7 R' is stated consistently on the two current official pages, but the meaning of 'R' is never explained, and the 2024 DICEA PDF wrote 'L7'. 9) PAGE FRESHNESS: the orientamento profile is labelled 'Updated on a.y. 2025/2026' and the program homepage still says 'Lectures start on 15th September 2025', while the admission page has clearly been updated for 2026 (CEnT-S, SAT, Jan-May 2026 window). Data for this record was taken from the more recently updated admission page where they conflict. 10) TECHNICAL NOTE: https://www.civil-environmental.unina.it/ served an EXPIRED TLS certificate at the time of research (GEANT OV RSA CA 4, issued to www.civil-environmental.unina.it, valid 2024-12-12 to 2025-12-11). The certificate subject matches the official unina.it hostname, so the site identity is genuine, but standard fetching tools reject it; content was retrieved with certificate validation disabled. 11) PROGRAM TYPE: confirmed type 'standalone' - this is a fully English degree awarded under its English name, not an English curriculum inside an Italian-named program, so no separate Italian diploma name applies. 12) No unina.it page indicates any relation of this program to the national 'semestre filtro' procedure (which concerns medicine/veterinary/architecture), and no interview or portfolio is required.
